_doc: Static cluster registry — used when CLUSTERS_CONFIG_FILE points to this file.
No hub Kubernetes cluster is required. The portal reads this file at startup.
Copy this file to clusters.json and fill in values for your environment.
PINNIPED CONCIERGE — TWO AUTHENTICATION MODES
Documentation: https://pinniped.dev/docs/reference/supported-clusters/
Pinniped Concierge operates in one of two modes depending on what the
cluster supports. The api_server URL and CA bundle SOURCE differ per mode.
── Mode A: Impersonation Proxy (default, works on ALL clusters) ───────────
Concierge runs its own HTTPS server that intercepts all kubectl/client
requests. It generates its own CA — completely separate from the cluster
CA in your kubeconfig.
api_server      → Concierge impersonation proxy LoadBalancer endpoint
ca_bundle_base64→ Pinniped-generated CA from CredentialIssuer status
(NOT the cluster CA from kubeconfig)
concierge_endpoint → same as api_server
Get both values from CredentialIssuer (single source of truth):
Endpoint:
kubectl get credentialissuer \
-o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.strategies[?(@.type=="ImpersonationProxy")].frontend.impersonationProxyInfo.endpoint}'
CA (already base64 — use directly as ca_bundle_base64):
kubectl get credentialissuer \
-o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.strategies[?(@.type=="ImpersonationProxy")].frontend.impersonationProxyInfo.certificateAuthorityData}'
Alternatively read directly from the auto-generated Secret:
kubectl get secret pinniped-concierge-impersonation-proxy-ca-certificate \
-n pinniped-concierge \
-o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}'
── Mode B: Direct KubeAPI / Aggregation Layer ─────────────────────────────
Concierge registers TokenCredentialRequest through the Kubernetes API
aggregation layer. Requires kube-apiserver to expose the aggregation
layer (kube-controller-manager must be running and accessible).
Common on full distributions (kubeadm, EKS, GKE). Often unavailable
on lightweight distros (K3s, K0s) without extra configuration.
api_server      → real kube-apiserver URL (same as in kubeconfig)
ca_bundle_base64→ cluster CA from kubeconfig (standard certificate-authority-data)
concierge_endpoint → same as api_server
Get both values from kubeconfig:
Endpoint:
kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.server}'
CA (already base64 — use directly as ca_bundle_base64):
kubectl config view --raw --minify -o jsonpath='{.clusters[0].cluster.certificate-authority-data}'
── How to check which mode is active on your cluster ──────────────────────
kubectl get credentialissuer -o json | grep -A5 '"type"'
Look for strategy.status = "Success" — that is the active mode.
ImpersonationProxy success → use Mode A values.
KubeClusterSigningCertificate success → use Mode B values.
Both can be active simultaneously; use Mode A values when in doubt.

clusters._doc: ── Mode A: Impersonation Proxy (most common — K3s, K0s, kubeadm without aggregation) ──
clusters._f_id: REQUIRED — unique identifier used in API paths (/api/v1/clusters/{id}/...).
clusters._f_name: OPTIONAL — display name in the Portal UI. Defaults to id.
clusters.name: My Cluster
_f_api_server: REQUIRED — Concierge impersonation proxy endpoint (NOT the kube-apiserver port 6443).
_f_ca_bundle_base64: REQUIRED — Pinniped's auto-generated CA for the impersonation proxy.
This is NOT the cluster CA from your kubeconfig.
The value is already base64-encoded — paste it directly here.
Preferred: read from CredentialIssuer status (matches api_server exactly):
Alternative: read from the auto-generated Secret in the Concierge namespace:
Note: Pinniped generates and rotates this CA automatically.
If using cert-manager instead, the Secret name may differ — check:
kubectl get secrets -n pinniped-concierge | grep ca
clusters.ca_bundle_base64: <paste base64 CA from CredentialIssuer or Secret>
_f_audience: Must match spec.audience in the JWTAuthenticator CR on this spoke cluster.
Each cluster MUST have a unique audience — reusing audiences across clusters
_f_jwt_authenticator_name: REQUIRED for /credentials (Concierge TokenCredentialRequest → short-lived mTLS cert).
Must match metadata.name of the JWTAuthenticator CR.
_f_issuer_url: OPTIONAL — Pinniped Supervisor FederationDomain issuer URL.
Required for /kubeconfig to emit a pinniped CLI exec-credential kubeconfig.
_f_concierge_endpoint: OPTIONAL — endpoint the pinniped CLI uses for TokenCredentialRequest.
In impersonation proxy mode this is the same as api_server.
Only set explicitly when the two addresses differ (e.g. internal vs external DNS).
_f_upstream_idp_name: OPTIONAL — upstream IDP name registered in the Pinniped Supervisor.
Passed as --upstream-identity-provider-name to the pinniped CLI.
_f_upstream_idp_type: OPTIONAL — must match the CR kind of upstream_idp_name.
Accepted values: oidc | ldap | activedirectory | github

clusters._doc: ── Mode B: Direct KubeAPI / Aggregation Layer (kubeadm, EKS, GKE, etc.) ──
_f_api_server: In aggregation layer mode, api_server is the real kube-apiserver URL —
same value as in your kubeconfig.
clusters.name: Production Cluster
_f_ca_bundle_base64: In aggregation layer mode the CA is the standard cluster CA from kubeconfig.
_f_concierge_endpoint: In aggregation layer mode, concierge_endpoint is the same kube-apiserver URL.
Omit or set equal to api_server.
